guia.what: Keeps a fixed aspect ratio for its content—images, video, iframes, maps—so nothing jumps while it loads. The ratio goes in `data-ts-ratio`; the direct child fills the box.
whenUse: You’re embedding media of unknown size and don’t want the layout to jump.
Every piece in a grid has to have the same shape.
It’s an embed (video, map) that needs a proportional box.
whenAvoid: The image has a known fixed height, so you don’t need it.
It’s text content. The text sets the height.
dos: Choose the ratio based on the real content (16/9 for video, 1/1 for portraits).
Combine it with `skeleton` if the media takes a while to arrive.
donts: Don’t use it to crop something that needs to be seen in full.
Don’t add several children. The direct child is the one that fills the box.

nucleo: The ratio is a continuous value. The stylesheet reads it from `--ts-aspect-ratio`, and Core writes that variable. Until Core runs, only 1 and 16/9 render correctly, because they also have their own class (`ts aspect-square`, `aspect-video`). Any other ratio renders square. Pass the ratio in `data-ts-ratio="1.3333"` on the element. Core copies it to `--ts-aspect-ratio` on init and whenever the attribute changes. There’s no interaction—it only sets the value at rest.
